channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Hold Nationwide Election Infrastructure Test on November 18
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will conduct a nationwide test of its election infrastructure on November 18. Citizens will be able to check their data in voter lists, undergo biometric identification, and familiarize themselves with the voting procedure. This event is part of preparations for upcoming presidential elections.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Meets with Pakistan's Army Chief in Islamabad
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, met with Pakistan's Army Chief, Asim Munir, in Islamabad. The meeting, held on Monday evening, focused on regional and international developments, bilateral relations, and strengthening cooperation to maintain peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Pakistan and Iran Discuss Afghanistan Developments and Regional Issues
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadeq, met with Iran's counterpart, Mohammad Reza Bahrami, in Islamabad. They discussed the latest developments in Afghanistan, regional issues, and exchanged views on matters of mutual interest. Both sides stressed the importance of continued dialogue.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Half of Afghan Children Face Severe Food Poverty
item.description: UNICEF states that half of Afghanistan's children suffer from severe food poverty and lack access to nutritious diets. While treating malnutrition saves lives, prevention is crucial. Around 3.7 million children experienced acute malnutrition in 2026, with 80% of those suffering from wasting being under two years old.

item.title: Ebola Death Toll Rises in the Democratic Republic of Congo
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded over 11,300 confirmed Ebola cases since May 2026, with 5,568 resulting in death, according to the National Institute of Public Health. The fatality rate stands at 48.9%, with the Ituri province most affected. No certified vaccines exist for this variant.

item.title: Russia Includes Central Asia in Demands for Ukraine War Settlement, NYT Reports
item.description: Russia has presented the US and European nations with demands for ending the war in Ukraine, which also concern Central Asia, according to a non-paper obtained by The New York Times. Russia seeks NATO to cease military activity in the region and revert to pre-1997 borders.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Head Saguimbaev Resigns Amidst Corruption Probe
item.description: Ermek Saguimbaev has been dismissed as head of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB). The official reason cited is a transition to another job and the need for leadership rotation. However, the president reportedly considered missteps by security forces in a corruption incident. Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new KNB head.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Officially Welcomed in Oman
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received an official welcome ceremony in Oman. Following the ceremony, a high-level meeting between the leaders of the two countries commenced. The welcome included a 21-gun salute in honor of the Uzbek president.

item.title: Belarusian Center for SCO People's Diplomacy Established in Minsk
item.description: A Belarusian Center for People's Diplomacy of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) has been established in Minsk, coinciding with the organization's 25th anniversary. The center aims to strengthen ties between peoples of SCO member states, with similar centers already operating in several countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Boost Economic Ties, Aiming for $500 Million in Trade
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman are expanding economic cooperation, with a goal to reach $500 million in bilateral trade. The sixth meeting of the Uzbek-Omani Joint Intergovernmental Commission in Muscat discussed reducing trade barriers and potential joint projects valued at $5 billion. This collaboration aims to leverage economic potential and attract Omani investments into Uzbekistan's industries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Transition to Electronic Certificates of Conformity
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is proposing to move its certificates and declarations of conformity to an electronic format. A draft resolution aims to simplify certification procedures, reduce administrative burdens on entrepreneurs, and further digitize the construction sector. Both electronic and paper formats will remain valid.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Cooperate on Cellular Therapy for Cancer Treatment
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding cooperation with China to implement innovative technologies for diagnosing and treating cancer. Discussions focused on introducing cellular therapies like CAR-T and CAR-NK. The Ministry of Health is exploring these advanced methods, which adapt immune cells to target cancer, requiring further research for clinical application in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Agreement with Uzbekistan on Pension Benefits in First Reading
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament has approved a bill to ratify an agreement with Uzbekistan on pension and social insurance. Signed in July 2026, the accord allows each country to independently manage pensions based on its laws, considering wages and contributions earned within its territory. Citizens can receive pensions even if they relocate.

item.title: IMF Downgrades Uzbekistan's Current Account Deficit Forecast for 2026
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has revised Uzbekistan's current account deficit forecast for 2026 from 3.2% to 5.1% of GDP. This adjustment is attributed to lower-than-expected gold exports and rapid import growth driven by high domestic demand. The IMF also projects Uzbekistan's economy to grow by 6.9% in 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Verify Accuracy of All Road Radars Amid Driver Complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan's traffic safety service will conduct a comprehensive check of all road radar devices due to complaints about inaccurate speed readings. Drivers have reported that some radars record speeds higher than actual. The verification aims to ensure fairness and legality in traffic law enforcement. Electronic traffic violation protocols are planned from 2027.

item.title: Central Asia Strengthens Position in Eurasian Economic Cooperation System
item.description: A forum in Shanghai discussed the transformation of international economic relations and Eurasian connectivity. Central Asia is shifting from a transit space to an active participant in Eurasian production and logistics chains, according to Bakhtiyor Mustafayev of ISMI. The expert emphasized the need to move from trade to joint investments and technology exchange, highlighting the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway as a priority.

item.title: Spy Scandal Surrounding Nvidia Complicates Trump's Asia Trip
item.description: US President Donald Trump's trip to Asia is overshadowed by a spy scandal involving Nvidia and recent midterm election losses. Reuters suggests this could complicate his talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The main topic for US-China discussions is the trade truce expiring in January, but the Nvidia scandal, involving alleged ties to Chinese intelligence, adds complexity. Beijing denies espionage accusations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Sector Reports Progress in Gasification and Oil Processing
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received a report on the energy sector's performance. By year-end, gasification will reach 64.5%, providing gas to 13.2 million citizens. Oil processing increased by 4.7%, and domestic bitumen production meets national demand. Investments are being made in refinery expansions and new petrochemical complexes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Imposes New Requirements for Cargo Shipments to Uzbekistan and Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's national railway company, "KTZ," has introduced new regulations for transporting goods to Uzbekistan and Afghanistan in wagons belonging to other railway administrations. These changes, effective November 13, aim to expedite the return of empty wagons to their countries of registration. The new rules apply to wagons of foreign rolling stock and require advance notification for empty wagon returns.

item.title: Two Greenhouses in Tashkent Region Caught Violating Coal Burning Regulations
item.description: During night raids in the Tashkent region, two greenhouses were found to be burning coal in violation of environmental requirements. The violations were discovered in the Tashkent and Zangiata districts. Administrative protocols have been filed, and owners were reminded of environmental laws. This follows a report on compensation for energy-saving technologies in greenhouses.

item.title: Gani Nygymetov Appointed Vice Minister of Science and Higher Education in Kazakhstan
item.description: Gani Nygymetov has been appointed Vice Minister of Science and Higher Education by government decree. Born in 1983 in the Aktobe region, he is a graduate of several universities, including L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University and the Monterey Institute of International Studies. His career includes roles in various government and educational institutions since 2003.

item.title: Uzbekistan Mandates Employer Protection Against Workplace Sexual Harassment
item.description: Uzbekistan has legally prohibited sexual harassment in the workplace, requiring employers to protect employees from unwanted sexual conduct. The labor code now includes a new article explicitly forbidding such actions, which include offensive comments, gestures, and unwanted touching.

item.title: Second Student Death at Kazakh National University Under Investigation
item.description: A first-year student has died in a dormitory at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University. Reports suggest hazing by senior students may be involved. The deceased student's relative claims the university initially reported a fever as the cause of death, but later admitted to a severe beating.

item.title: Wildberries Founder Tatyana Kim to Be Included in New EU Sanctions List
item.description: Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim will be added to the European Union's new sanctions list, according to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. The sanctions will affect 145 individuals and entities, including a St. Petersburg oil terminal. Wildberries is accused of operating as a supply network for the Russian military.

item.title: Kazakhstan Registers 1048 Medicinal Preparations, Streamlining Access
item.description: Kazakhstan has registered 1048 medicinal preparations since the start of the year, aiming to reduce administrative barriers and speed up patient access to modern drugs. A 'one-stop-shop' service implemented in 2026 has reduced registration time to 15 working days. Kazakhstan's registration numbers exceed those of Armenia, Belarus, and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Taliban Ministry Approves Detailed Development Plan for West Kabul Zone
item.description: The Taliban Ministry of Urban Development and Housing has approved a detailed development plan for the western zone of Kabul. The plan, covering 12,736 acres, includes residential plots, apartments, commercial spaces, two universities, two hospitals, and recreational areas. It aims to provide housing for 120,000 families and accommodate approximately 720,000 people.

item.title: Kazakhstan considers introducing photo identification for children under 16
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering introducing photo identification for children under 16. Currently, only birth certificates are mandatory, which lack sufficient information to uniquely identify a child. A parliamentary deputy raised concerns about child trafficking, prompting the Ministry of Education to form an interdepartmental commission to study the issue.

item.title: UN Secretary-General calls for prevention of autonomous weapons use and proliferation
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that autonomous weapons systems are politically unacceptable and morally repugnant, urging their prevention. He highlighted the new humanitarian, legal, ethical, and security challenges they pose and stressed the need to prioritize humanity and human life amidst intensifying global conflicts.

item.title: FAO allocates $2 million for agricultural businesses in Afghanistan
item.description: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has allocated $2 million to support agricultural businesses in Afghanistan through its Matching Grant Program, funded by the Asian Development Bank. The program aims to expand businesses and improve food security, with grants ranging from $5,000 to $30,000 available until November 30, 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Vice-Ministers for Science and Tourism
item.description: Kazakhstan has appointed new vice-ministers for Science and Higher Education, and for Tourism and Sports. Gani Nygymetov, formerly head of Almaty University of Power Engineering and Communications, is the new Vice-Minister of Science and Higher Education. Adilet Turganbayev, previously head of the gambling regulation committee, is the new Vice-Minister of Tourism and Sports.

item.title: Turkish Investor to Build Strawberry Greenhouses in Kazakhstan's Turkestan Region
item.description: Turkish company MIR AGRO KZ will construct a vegetable storage facility and greenhouses in the Turkestan region, investing 15.6 billion tenge. The project aims to produce up to 6,600 tons of strawberries annually, creating 30 permanent and 100 seasonal jobs. Construction is planned in phases for 2026-2027, starting with an 8,000-ton storage facility.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Receives Energy Minister's Report on Ten-Month Performance
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev was briefed on the energy sector's ten-month results, the heating season, and future plans. The heating season is proceeding normally across all regions. Electricity generation increased by 2.3% to 102.4 billion kWh, and oil processing rose by 4.7%.

item.title: Astana to Acquire Land for Second Phase of LRT Project
item.description: Astana's Akimat plans to acquire 0.3626 hectares of land in the Saryarka district for the construction of the second line of the Tarlan Astana light rail transit. The compulsory acquisition is expected to be completed by February 1, 2028.

item.title: Iran Offers to Transfer 2,000 MW of Electricity to Afghanistan
item.description: Iran's Minister of Energy has stated that Iran is ready to immediately transfer 2,000 MW of electricity to Afghanistan, provided the country's power grid is prepared for distribution. The minister also pledged full cooperation in energy sector investment and electricity transit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan committee approves bill to increase 'Batyr Ene' pension supplement to 5,000 soms
item.description: A parliamentary committee in Kyrgyzstan has approved a bill to raise the monthly pension supplement for mothers awarded the 'Batyr Ene' order from 1,000 to 5,000 soms. The increase aims to better support mothers amid rising living costs and align with a presidential decree.

item.title: Afghan intelligence highlights Sharia-based operations and Islamic system principles
item.description: Afghan intelligence officials discussed their institution's operations and adherence to Sharia law at a research conference. The General Directorate of Intelligence was noted as the first government body to have special regulations established. Officials emphasized combating crime and safeguarding human dignity under the Islamic system.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Reviews Energy Sector Performance and Heating Season
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received a report on the energy sector's performance over ten months and the ongoing heating season. The Minister of Energy stated that the heating season is proceeding stably across all regions. Investments in power plant repairs have increased, reducing the number of high-risk stations, and electricity generation has risen by 2.3%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Parliament Committee Approves Bill to Plant Five Trees for Each Cut
item.description: A committee of the Kyrgyz Parliament has approved a bill mandating the planting of five saplings for every tree felled, with a three-year care requirement. The legislation aims to protect green spaces, prohibit area reduction, and enhance measures against illegal logging. It also proposes digital inventory of trees.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev briefed on upcoming early maslikhat elections
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received a briefing on the preparations for early elections of maslikhat deputies. He emphasized the importance of conducting elections based on the constitutional principle of "Law and Order" and ensuring equal conditions for all candidates and parties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan extends commercial fishing ban on Issyk-Kul and Son-Kul lakes until 2029
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has extended the ban on commercial fishing in Issyk-Kul and Son-Kul lakes for three years, until 2029. This decision aims to preserve and increase fish stocks. Exceptions are made for artificial reproduction, sport fishing, scientific research, and ichthyological monitoring.
